description: Community Health and Resource Management (CHARM) is a web tool or resource listed in U.S. Climate Resilience Toolkit, a national climate-adaptation toolkit, published or maintained by Texas Community Watershed Partners; Texas A&M AgriLife Extension; Texas A&M University. CHARM gives local officials, stakeholders, and citizens talong the U.S. Gulf Coast he power to map and analyze growth with real-time feedback. Coverage: the United States, or as stated on the tool page. The toolkit lists hazards: Erosion and Shoreline Recession, Flooding – Coastal, Flooding – General, High Winds. Assets: Critical Facilities, Cultural and Community Services, Energy and Utilities, Natural Areas and Wildlife, Property, Transportation and Mobility, Urban Landscape and Tree Canopy, Water Infrastructure – General. It is reached through the links recorded on this page, with the catalogue entry as the discovery route. Access is free of charge and open. The licence is not stated on the toolkit page (no licence or terms statement seen). Caveats: this record was written from the toolkit page, which was read; the tool itself was not opened or run, its licence and current availability were not checked, and the description may lag the source. It can support climate-adaptation planning and exposure screening. Related record: the catalogue-level record data-us-climate-resilience-toolkit-catalogue.
